scope: Development and book counter-controls. Not held-out cases.

cases.source: 100 Endgame Patterns, personal reading PDF page60, Zamarbide-Benitez La Roda2005, White35g4? versus35Ke3!, diagram visually checked.
cases.history_limit: The diagram fixes the board and side. Earlier history and halfmove clock are unavailable; use zero for this research start, no repetition or fifty-move inference.
cases.human_task: Test whether immediately spending g3-g4 allows ...f6 and a king blockade, while Ke3 preserves g4 as a later waiting move to gain f5. The move order must matter against the opponent best replies, not only the book line.
falsifiers: If g4 still wins, reject the lost-win hypothesis.
If Ke3 does not win in bounded searches, do not assume the book judgment is proven.
Do not call one PV forced or equate a pawn-count difference with the waiting-move mechanism.

cases.source: John Doknjas, Opening Repertoire The Modern Benoni, PDF pages59-60 (printed58-59), Game7 variation12Nd2?!; successor12...Nb6 diagram visually checked.
cases.human_task: Nd2 supports e4 but withdraws the active f3 knight. Test whether ...Nb6 and the threat ...Nfxd5 make this natural defence inferior to Re1; explain the concrete enabled response and its cost.
falsifiers: Do not claim ...Nb6 forces material gain from one PV.
The queen on c2 and bishop on e2 must be tracked; an attack count is not a proof of an unanswerable threat.
If modern equal-depth analysis does not separate the alternatives, report the book hypothesis as unconfirmed.

cases.source: Book counter-control: opponent b3 reserve remains; early g4 still fails.
Book late use after Black spent b3: g4 gives way to Kf5.
Book spent-reserve state: legal king moves cannot simply take f5.
